The idea

A.R.E.S. in 60 seconds

Read these four cards and you have the whole project. The rest of the page lets you check each claim.

1The problem

Before anyone walks on Mars, planners must answer three questions: where can a crew land safely, how far can it roam and still get home, and what protects it on the way? The data that answers them sits in separate NASA products and files.

2Our answer

A.R.E.S. joins those layers into one connected mission at a reference site on Arcadia Planitia: a layered map, a 100 km two-crew EVA plan with a separate backup path, a suited Marswalk check, a four-crew habitat, a modular rover and the Earth-to-Mars transfer.

3What you can try

The numbers are live. Switch the operating mode and the route, energy and walk-back checks recompute. Fly the transfer, tour the base, pull the rover apart part by part. Every decision links to a source or is marked as an assumption.

4What we are honest about

AP-8 is a reference point, not a NASA selection. The planner runs on synthetic terrain until real raster exports are loaded, and the habitat and rover are student concepts. Every gap is listed under Evidence.

    The team

    Team AstroTec

    AstroTec · Team A.R.E.S.

    AstroTec is a student team from PrepaTec Querétaro focused on science, technology and space exploration. We are taking part in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge with a proposal for a habitable base on Mars. Our work covers researching the planet's resources and conditions, designing its facilities, and building an interactive platform where users can explore each area and learn what it is for, to help ensure the survival and safety of future astronauts.

          Limits & FAQ

          What this project is not, and the questions we expect.

          What is real, and what is synthetic?

          Site facts (position, elevation, ice and radar signals, the 2021 landing-site downselect) come from published NASA, JPL and USGS work and are tagged with their sources. The EVA planner's terrain is generated until a real 520 × 520 grid is loaded from Mars Trek, HiRISE, THEMIS and SWIM exports. Radiation scaling and walk rules are proxies. The Evidence tab sorts every input into real, proxy or synthetic.

          Is AP-8 a NASA choice?

          No. NASA has not selected a Mars base location. AP-8 is a reference point inside the 2021 JPL/SpaceX Starship downselect (Golombek et al.). The site matrix lets you weigh the criteria yourself.

          Are the habitat and rover flight-ready?

          No. They are proposed concepts for a student competition. Eleven open places where the vehicle datasheet, the 3D files and the planner defaults disagree or leave a gap are listed openly, each with a next step (a twelfth, the radiation figure, is resolved).

          Do I need to install or sign in to anything?

          No. The whole atlas is one HTML file that runs in a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. The 3D tools need WebGL. The first load of the Map & EVA scene takes a few seconds.

          Can I keep a copy of the results?

          Yes. Evidence · Export downloads the mission package and planner route as JSON and prints the evidence pages to PDF. This guide can also be printed.

          What would you do next?

          Load real Mars Trek, HiRISE, THEMIS and SWIM rasters into the planner and the helmet HUD, settle the open decisions (D1 to D9, D11 and D12), and replace the simplified transfer with a real launch window.

          Not an official NASA decision. NASA has not chosen a Mars base location. The three sites come from the 2021 JPL/SpaceX Starship downselect (Golombek et al.); later work, including by NASA researchers, studied them further. "Safest" and "strongest ice" are within-group statements. Ice depth is inferred from orbital data and morphology, not measured.

          NASA data

          NASA data connection

          Every NASA product and published NASA result the project draws on: what A.R.E.S. takes from it, where you can see it, whether it enters as a real value, a proxy or a synthetic stand-in, and where to open it at NASA. This is the answer to the Space Apps field "NASA data".

          REAL: a published value or algorithm used as it is. PROXY: a real signal turned into a score or scaled with an assumed rule. SYNTHETIC: generated by code until real rasters are loaded. PLANNED: the step that replaces synthetic terrain. Details for the planner are in .

          Real, proxy or synthetic

          Which inputs come from real NASA products, which are proxies and which are generated. No dataset measures subsurface ice directly; SWIM scores how consistently several indirect signals agree.

            About the A.R.E.S. Mission Atlas

            Team AstroTec's final delivery for the NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map, gathered into one page. New here? Start with the Guide tab or press the tour button.

            • Guide: judges' start page: 60-second summary, 5-minute tour, criteria map, team, references, submission details.
            • Mission: the thread through all tools, with a live dashboard.
            • Transfer: the A.R.E.S-1 Earth to Mars simulation.
            • Site brief: challenge response, site matrix, data layers, terrain units.
            • Map & EVA: landing pad screening, eight layers, double-path route, rover simulation, suited Marswalk, spec checks.
            • Helmet HUD: a first-person walk on the AP-8 plain with what a suited astronaut would read: Mars time and Sun, Earth link, suit and vitals, walk-back margin, radiation and alerts.
            • Habitat: 3D base with systems, energy, safety drills and a guided tour.
            • Vehicles: numbered 3D parts, the V23 datasheet variables and a calculator.
            • Evidence: coverage, NASA data connection, data status, open decisions, sources, submission checklist, export.

            Keys: 1 to 9 switch views, Ctrl/⌘ + K opens quick jump, Esc closes this panel.

            Limits. A concept for a student competition, not an official NASA selection and not flight-qualified. The planner terrain is synthetic until a real 520 × 520 grid (250 m cells) is loaded from Mars Trek, HiRISE, THEMIS and SWIM exports. The 3D habitat and vehicle shapes are illustrative; part names in the vehicle files were read from geometry and need checking against the CAD tree. This page is not endorsed by NASA and uses no NASA logos.

            Hosting. One HTML file of about 3.0 MB with no other files to keep together. It needs a modern browser with WebGL and gzip streams (current Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari).
